lines.text: Do you know how your phone turns your voice into a file?
You hum a little tune into a voice note. To the phone, your voice is just air, wobbling back and forth.
Those wobbles hit a tiny diaphragm inside the mic, far thinner than a hair, and it shakes right along.
Every shake becomes a tiny change in voltage. A wave of electricity, shaped exactly like your voice.
Then the phone measures that wave about forty eight thousand times a second, and writes each one down as a number.
Line up all those numbers, squeeze them smaller, and that's your file.
Then Orbi Transfer sends it. Locked on your phone, it pops up on your friend's screen nearby, and they hear you hum.
